The man holds out the oar to you, but your hands are full.

You see the young man, about 41 ft away, do this. In his words: "Step close to the mirror, square up in front of it, and carefully study my reflection: face, eyes, hair, build, any scars, moles, tan lines, or tattoos. Open my mouth to check teeth, turn side to side, and look at my hands and nails for calluses or ink stains."

You see the young man, about 0 ft away, do this. In his words: "Touch the glass with fingertips to feel temperature and check for any give, watch my reflection for any lag as I move my hand, then gently lift and angle the mirror away from the tree to look along the edges and behind the frame for markings, hinges, or hidden compartments."

You see the young man, about 0 ft away, do this. In his words: "Stand centered directly in front of the mirror and look into it, raising my right hand to wave and touch the glass. Then step quickly to the left out of the mirror’s view, wait a beat, and lean back into view again, watching closely for what I see while she watches what changes."

You see the young man, about 0 ft away, do this. In his words: "Stand squarely in front of the mirror and stare into it, focusing on what’s shown. Note whether I see myself or a small figure (clothes, background, movement). Raise my right hand to wave, then my left, lean closer, and touch the glass, watching for any response or lag. Shift a step left, then right, to see if the image tracks me."

The young man, right next to you, does this to you. In his words: "I nod emphatically to her, point toward the bell on the headland, mime pulling a rope to ring it, give a thumbs‑up, then turn and start carefully descending the ladder."

The young man, right next to you, does this to you. In his words: "Keeping both hands on the rungs, I meet her eyes, then turn my head to look toward the stone circle she indicated and give a small nod."

You see the young man, about 5 ft away, do this. In his words: "Step carefully into the center of the stone circle, stand still with the lantern down at my side, and take a slow turn, listening and looking for any change—sound, wind, light, or movement. Then look down at the grass for any pattern or depression and feel the ground with my bare foot for warmth or vibration."

reflections.text: I'm standing on sand, naked, with a journal and a pencil and no idea how I got here. There's a boat just up the beach. I'll look at that first.

The boat looks sound, and there's an oar in it. If I came in on this, I don't remember it. I'll take the oar and then head for that cabin — being naked out here, I want something between me and the open beach.
Oar's heavier than it looks. Hands are full now — journal, pencil, this. I'll walk north toward the cabin and see if anyone's there, or if there's anything to wear.
Grass underfoot now. There's a fire pit ahead, stones and old ashes, and a wheelbarrow off to the left. Still no one calling out. I'll keep going to the door.
Someone else is out there, northeast, walking. Too far to see clearly. I'll call out before they get farther away.
No answer. Either they didn't hear me, or they don't want to be found. The cabin door is close. I'll go there and see if the chest has anything useful.
Door's right here, latch on it. Nobody answered my shout. I'll try the latch before I go digging in the chest.
The door opens. Inside there's a bed with a wool blanket, a swept fireplace, and a lantern on the table. Nobody home. The blanket is the first thing I want — I'm still naked.

The bed is made, blanket folded over a straw mattress. I'll look closer and see if I can take the blanket without wrecking the whole thing. My hands are already full, so I may have to set the oar down.
The bed's empty of anyone, but that blanket is the only cloth I've seen. I'll set the oar down so I can take it.
Oar's down. Now the blanket — if it comes free, I'll wrap it around myself.
The blanket won't come off. It's part of the bed, not something I can take. The chest outside might have clothes or something else I can use. I'll go look.
There's a young man, naked like me, walking northeast of the cabin. Close enough to see now. I'll call to him before I go any nearer.
He's closer now, maybe sixty feet off, still walking. I'll finish the shout and see if he turns.
He didn't answer. He's still walking, about fifty feet off, naked like me. I'll go closer and try again before he moves on.
I reached where he was, but he's already moved — southwest, back toward the cabin, still walking, still not answering. I'll follow.
He's heading west, toward the cabin, same as I was. Naked, journal and pencil, just like me. I'll keep after him and try speaking once I'm close enough that a shout isn't the only option.
He's stopped. Standing now, not walking — naked, journal and pencil, same as me. Almost there. I'll finish closing the distance, then talk.
He's right by the open door, looking at something, still not acknowledging me. Close enough to talk without shouting. I'll try.
He didn't answer. Eighteen feet and not a word — either he didn't hear me or he doesn't want to. I'll get closer and see what he's doing before I try again.
He just tried the same thing I did — pull the blanket off the bed and wrap it around himself. It didn't work for me. I'll get close enough to tell him that, and ask if he remembers anything.
I'm right beside him now. He's talking, but I didn't catch words on the way in. Same situation as me — naked, journal, pencil, and he just tried the blanket too. I'll speak to him plainly.
He's right here, talking, but I still haven't heard a word I can answer. I'll wait a moment and see if he actually replies.

He answered. Same as me — no memory. He thinks he's wrapped in the blanket and that I'm still outside. From here he's still naked, and I'm already standing next to him. I'll tell him that, and that the chest is fine to open.
Still saying it. He isn't in sight in this moment — maybe he stepped toward the door while I was talking. I'll finish, then look.
He's gone from the room. I finished talking to empty air. I'll look around and see which way he went, then the chest.
He's gone. No sound of him leaving, just not here. We said we'd open the chest. I'll go do that, and look for him on the way out.
He's outside now, southeast, walking — toward the chest, maybe. I'll keep going and meet him there.
The chest is already open. Not clothes — gold, a heap of it, almost to the brim. Useless for being naked, but he should see it. I'll tell him.
He didn't answer, and he's not in sight. The coins are right here. I'll take a handful and see if they're real before I go looking for him.
The coins are real enough — heavy, cold in my hand. He still hasn't answered. I'll call once more, then look for him instead of standing here with a fortune I can't wear.
No answer. He was just west of me, then gone. I'll check the cabin before I wander into the trees.
I hear him. He's inside, by the table, with the lantern, asking about clothes or tools. I'll get to the door and answer him from there.
He asked what I found. I'll answer from the doorway so he can hear me, then go in.
Still telling him what I found. I'll finish, then go in.
He's inside, looking at something, lantern in hand. His journal is on the table. I said I'd come in — I'll go to him.
Almost at the door. He's still inside with the lantern. I'll go in and talk where we can actually see each other.
The hearth is empty. He's a few steps away, still moving, lantern in hand. I'll tell him what I see and ask what he found.
He didn't answer out loud. He's by the table, setting something down. I'll go over so we aren't talking across the room.
We're finally in the same spot. He put the lantern on the bed. I'll talk to him directly instead of across the room.
He just tried to hand me the oar, and my hands are full — journal, pencil, coins. I'll finish what I'm saying, then decide whether I even want it.
He tried to hand me the oar and my hands were full. I still don't know why. I'll ask before I clear a hand for it.
I asked him why the oar. He hasn't answered yet. I'll give him a moment before I clear a hand or take it.
He's walking off with the lantern and didn't answer. The oar is on the bed now. I'll follow him rather than stand here waiting.
We're face to face again and he still hasn't said a word I can hear. I'll try once more, shorter, and wait to see if he answers.
He finally answered. He wants the coins and journals on the table, just the lantern, and the mirror. I'll go with him. A mirror might tell us something a chest of gold won't.
I'm telling him yes. Once that's out, I'll set my things on the table and go with him.
He wants the coins and journals left here. I'll put mine on the table, then follow him to the mirror.
At the table. I'll leave the coins first, then the journal and pencil, and go after him.
Coins are on the table. Journal next, then the pencil, then I'll catch up with him.
Pencil last. Then I'll find him and the mirror.
Hands are empty. He's not in the room. I'll look for him before I wander off toward a mirror I can't see from here.
He's already gone. The door is open. I'll go out and look for him and the mirror before I lose him in the trees.
The mirror is west, a bit over a hundred feet, against a tree. He's not in sight. I'll go there and hope he meant it.
He's ahead of me, west, right by the mirror. I'll keep going.
He's already at the mirror, lantern on the ground beside him. I'll keep walking.
He's studying his own reflection — face, hands, all of it. I'll be there in a moment and do the same.
I'm at the mirror with him. He's been studying his face. I want to see mine too — maybe there's a mark, a scar, anything that tells me who I am.
The glass is clean, but looking at the frame didn't show me my face. I'll step in front of it and actually look.
He's checking the glass itself now — temperature, lag, the back of the frame. I'll finish looking at my face first.
Still looking. I want to know what the glass shows before I start poking at the frame.
The mirror didn't show me anything when I studied it that way. He was talking. I'll try using the glass, and ask him what he sees.
The glass didn't show me. It showed someone else — small, in a red shirt and blue trousers, looking back. That isn't this body. I need to tell him.

He asked if I see anything strange. I'm already telling him. The figure in the glass doesn't match either of us — we're both naked, and it was dressed. I'll finish saying that before I decide on the boat or the tower.
I told him. I'll wait a moment for what he sees before I pick the boat or the tower.
He's talking right beside me. I'll stay quiet a few more seconds and see if he answers about the figure in the glass.
He didn't answer. Maybe he didn't hear me over his own talking. I'll say it again, shorter, and ask him to look with me.
Still nothing back. He's right here with a pencil. I'll ask once more, plainly, before I decide anything else.
He's testing it — waving, stepping out of view, leaning back. I'll watch the glass while he moves.
Same figure again. It didn't wave or step aside with him. It just looked back, dressed, small. That isn't either of us. I'll tell him before we leave this.
He's testing it again — waving, shifting left and right. I'll finish telling him what I already saw, then watch the glass while he moves.
He's testing the glass again, waving and shifting. I'll finish telling him what I saw, then listen.
He still hasn't said what he sees. I'll ask once more, then I'd rather go to the tower than keep staring at a glass that won't show us.
He's talking again, but I still don't hear words. I'll finish what I'm saying and give him a moment.
He still hasn't answered. I said I was going. The platform is the one place I can't see from here, so that's where I'm headed. He can follow if he wants.
He's with me, a few feet off, lantern and pencil in hand. Good. I'll keep going toward the tower.
He's still with me, lantern in hand. The bridge is ahead, then the tower. I'll keep going.
He's still with me. There's a stepladder in the grass I didn't notice before, and a stone circle farther east, but the tower is what I came for. I'll keep walking.
Almost there. He's still with me. I'll see what's on the platform once I can climb.
The rungs look solid. I came this far to see the platform, so I'm going up. He can follow if he wants.
He's climbing too, a little below me. The lantern stayed on the grass. I'll keep going up.
Halfway-ish up, and he's still with me. I'll keep climbing until I can see the platform.
Thirty-eight feet up. He's just below me. I'll keep climbing.
Halfway. The island looks smaller already — cabin, boat, the bell on the headland. I'll keep going.
Sixty-six feet. The platform is close. I'll keep climbing.
Almost there. I'll see the platform in a moment.
I can see the platform now. There's a table with a lighter, a sword in a scabbard, and a snorkel with a mask. I'll finish the climb.
I'm up. The whole island is under me, and the table has a lighter, a sword in a scabbard, and a snorkel. He's almost here. I'll look at the sword first.
He's up, and he already took the lighter. The sword and the snorkel are still on the table. I'll tell him what I see and ask if the lighter works.
He has the lighter and the sword now, and still no answer I can hear. The snorkel is the last thing on the table. I'll take it, then try to get a response from him some other way than talking.
He's right here and still silent. I'll ask for something simple — a nod — before I decide whether to go back down.
Words aren't getting an answer. I'll wave in front of him and point toward the stone circle, and watch whether he reacts at all.
He nodded. He pointed at the bell, mimed ringing it, and started down. So he can hear me. I'll follow him.
He's still above me on the ladder. I'll keep going down, then head for the bell like he showed me.
He nodded at the stone circle too. I'll finish the climb down, then decide between the bell and the stones.
Still going down. The stones are closer than the bell. I'll look at them first once I'm on the ground.
I'm ahead of him on the way down. I'll keep going and walk to the stones once I reach the grass.
Almost halfway down. The stones are the closer thing he nodded at. I'll go there first.
Twenty-four feet left. I'll finish the descent and walk to the stones.
Almost on the ground. The stones are about a minute's walk northeast. I'll go there and wait if he follows.
The lantern can stay. The stones are closer, and he nodded at them. I'll walk there and look at the ring.
He's still on the ladder. I'll keep going to the stones and look at the ring when I get there.
The ring is right ahead. I'll look at the stones when I reach them.
The ring is just stones and grass from here. I'll look closer for markings before I decide about the bell. He's shouting back by the tower, but I can't make out the words.
He shouted that he's coming here with the lantern and the lighter. I'll finish looking at the stones and wait for him.
Nothing marked that I can see. He's on his way. I'll shout so he knows I'm already here, then look at the stones while I wait.
He's closer now, walking this way. I'll finish the shout and keep looking at the ring.
He's still a minute off. I'll walk the ring and look at the joints between the stones for anything cut into them.
He's close now. I'll finish the circuit of the stones before he gets here.
The ring is just fitted stones. He's almost here. I'll meet him and see if he still wants the bell.
He's right here now. I'll tell him the stones are plain and ask if he still wants the bell.
He's busy with something and hasn't answered. I'll look at what he's doing before I head for the bell alone.
He still isn't answering. The bell was his idea, and there's time. I'll walk there and he can follow if he wants.
He's checking the middle of the ring. I'll keep going to the bell and look at it myself.
He's following. The bell is just ahead. I'll look at it when I get there.
The rope is right there. I'll look at the bell before I pull it, in case the frame is loose.
He said he's ringing it. I'll cover my ears.
I didn't hear a ring. I'll look at the bell and see if he pulled the rope.
The bell rang, loud, right here. I'll finish looking at it and see if anything answers.
The bell rang and nothing else answered. I'll wait and listen before I decide whether to ring it again.
Nothing answered the bell. I'll ask him what he wants to do with the time left.
I asked him what he wants to do. I'll give him a moment to answer before I walk to the cliffs.
He's talking. I'll stay and listen.
He walked off toward the cliffs without answering. I'll follow and see where he's going.
He's at the cliff edge, looking at something. I'll go see what it is, and stop short of the drop.
We're at the edge. I'll look over it carefully and see what's below.
That didn't show me the drop. I'll step closer to the edge and look at the water myself.
Almost at the edge. I'll stop there and look out.
The edge stopped me. I'll look out and see the water from here.
The water is just past the edge. I'll step as close as I can and look at it before the time runs out.
I can't step into the water. I'll look at the cliffs from here and stay put.
The rocks drop straight into the surf. I won't climb. I'll sit and watch the water until this ends.
The surf is right below the rocks. I'll stay sitting and watch it until the time runs out.

reflections.text: Okay. I’m on a hilltop, naked and jittery. First I just want to really take in what’s around me—sky, wind, any movement or sounds—before I pick a direction. I’ll scan the area carefully.
Water first. I’ll head to the stream and see what it’s like—maybe drink, maybe just listen.
Almost there. I’m thirsty and also curious if it’s clear and moving fast.
I’ll check the stream—how clear it is, how fast it’s moving, any smell—before I try a sip.
It looks clean. I’ll kneel, cup my hands, take a cautious sip, then splash my face and neck.
That helped. I’m still uneasy being naked. The cabin might have clothes or tools. I’ll head there.
There’s someone out there. I don’t want to meet them naked in the open. I’ll slip to the forest edge for cover and watch a moment.
I don’t want to be seen like this. I’ll grab a leafy branch for cover before moving on.
Hold on—quiet and quick. If she comes closer I’ll stay behind cover.
I’ll let her know I’m here but ask for space while I try to find something to wear. Then I’ll head toward the cabin, keeping to cover where I can.
I’m heading to the cabin to find something to wear!
I see a chest by the door—maybe clothes. I’ll keep going.
She’s naked too. Okay. I’ll just get to the chest by the door and see if there’s anything wearable.
I’m going to check this chest for clothes.
I’ll keep going—get to the chest first, then try to open it.
Inside—grab the blanket to cover up.
Yes! I’m inside—give me a moment.
Blanket first—cover up.
Just checking the blanket—then I’ll wrap it around me.
I’m grabbing the blanket—one second.
Almost covered—then I’ll answer her.

I hear you. I woke up with no memory too. I don’t know what’s going on. I’m inside the cabin now with a blanket around my waist. Are you okay? If you’re comfortable, you can come in, or I can check the chest by the door for clothes for us. I won’t come closer unless you say it’s okay.
She’s right here. Okay—finish what I’m saying, then I want to try that chest by the door for clothes or anything useful.
I’ll finish, then ask if she’s okay being inside with me and suggest I check that chest for clothes.
I don’t remember anything either. I’m going to check that chest by the door for clothes or anything useful—want to wait here a sec?
Almost there—if it opens, I’ll see what’s inside.
I’m going to open this chest—maybe there’s clothing or tools.
Thanks—opening it now. Let’s see what’s inside.
It’s full of gold—no clothes. I’m coming back inside so we can search properly for anything useful. I’ll keep some space unless you want me closer.
Heading back in—let’s search the cabin together for anything to wear. I’ll check shelves and crates first.
Let’s search inside together. I’ll check the table and fireplace for anything useful.
I’ll check the table and fireplace. If you find anything, shout.
I saw—gold, no clothes. I’m checking the table and lantern.
I’m at the table—there’s a lantern here, half-full of oil. Grabbing it.
I picked up a lantern. I’m by the table inside. I’m going to check the fireplace for matches or anything useful. Do you see anything out there—any clothes or tools?
Let me finish saying that, then I’ll search the fireplace for tinder or tools. After, I’ll set the journal and pencil on the table to free a hand.
I’m inside—by the table. I’m going to check the fireplace for matches, then I’ll come to you.
Setting my journal down, then I’ll check the fireplace.
I’m inside by the table—checking the fireplace for matches, then I’ll come to the door.
I’m by the fireplace—checking it now. It looks swept. I see an oar on the floor; I’ll grab it next. Any luck on your side?
Checking the fireplace—looks empty so far. After this I’ll grab the oar. You okay there?
Fireplace is empty. I’m going to grab the oar—glad you’re coming in.
Oar right here—I’ll grab it, then set the lantern on the table so I’ve got hands free.
I’ll set the lantern on the bed and grab the oar.
I’m here—setting the lantern down so I can grab the oar. Fireplace looks empty. After that, we can check the boat or the mirror—any preference?
I’ll grab the oar so we have at least one tool in hand.
Grabbing the oar—then maybe we check that mirror together.
Fireplace’s empty. I found this lantern and the oar. Could you carry the oar? Then I’ll grab the lantern, and we can go look at that mirror together.
Your hands are full—could you set the coins on the table so you can take the lantern? I’ll set the oar on the bed now, then grab the lantern and we can go look at the mirror.
I’m setting the oar down. Do you want to set your coins and journal on the table so you can take the lantern? Or I can carry the lantern and we leave the coins here for now.
I found the lantern and the oar; fireplace’s empty. If you set the coins on the table, you could take the oar. I’ll carry the lantern. Want to check the mirror together?
I’ve got the lantern. If you set your coins on the table, could you take the oar? Let’s go check that mirror together.

The oar’s just a useful tool for now—and for the boat later. Let’s check the mirror first, then the boat. If you’re okay, set the coins and journal on the table to free your hands; I’ll carry the lantern.
At the door with the lantern. I want to see the mirror next.
I’ll finish saying that, then head to the mirror to the west with the lantern.
No name. After this finishes, I’ll head to the mirror with the lantern. Let’s leave the coins here.
No—no name. I’m going to the mirror now. Come with me? We can leave the coins here for later.
No—I don’t have a name. Come on, let’s go look at the mirror.
Thanks—meet me at the mirror. I’ve got the lantern.
Heading west to the mirror with the lantern—meet you there.
Almost there—heading to the mirror with the lantern.
Almost to the mirror—still heading there with the lantern.
Here at the mirror—looking at it.
I’m going to set the lantern down and look closely at my reflection.
Maybe my face will jog something. I’ll get right in front of the mirror and study myself closely.
Maybe something on my skin will jog a memory. I’ll keep looking closely.
I’m at the mirror—checking if there’s anything written on it or behind it.
She’s right here now. The mirror felt normal; no markings behind it. I’ll talk to her, then maybe suggest boat or tower next.
Our reflections look normal to me. If you’re up for it, I’d like to head to the tower for a better view of the island. We can come back for the boat after. I’ll grab the lantern—want to walk with me?
Let’s head to the tower for a look around. I’ve got the lantern—walk with me?
I saw myself before. That’s strange. I’m stepping back to the mirror now—tell me if what you see changes as I move.
I’m coming back. Earlier I saw myself. While you’re looking, I’ll step in and out of view to see if it changes—can you describe the figure more?
Okay—stand centered and keep watching. I’ll set the lantern down, then move in and out of the mirror’s view and touch the glass. Tell me exactly what changes.
I’m going to test it—watch and tell me exactly what you see as I move.
Watching closely—tell me exactly what you see as I move.
I’m looking now—tell me if the figure changes as I move.
I’m going to look again now and tell you exactly what I see.
I’m looking straight into it now. What I see might be different from you—what is the small figure doing? Does it copy my wave?
This mirror is weird, and I want to figure it out before moving on.
I saw myself earlier. I’m coming with you now—bringing the lantern.
I’m with you. Let’s go to the tower—lantern in hand. We can check the island from up high.
I’m with you—let’s stick together to the tower. If you see anything odd, say so.
Sticking with you. If the ladder looks solid, we’ll climb—lantern first if it’s dim up there.
Still with you—let’s keep to the ladder. Once we’re there, we’ll check if it’s sturdy before climbing.
Almost there. At the base I’ll test the rungs; if it feels solid I’ll climb. Are you okay with heights?
Almost there. When we reach the base, I’ll test the rungs. If they’re solid, I’ll climb first with the lantern.
The rungs look solid. I’ll climb up first and see what’s on the platform. I’ll leave the lantern here for now—daylight’s fine. Follow if you’re comfortable.
I’ll climb after you—keeping a few rungs below. Tell me if you see anything up there.
Climbing just below you—take your time. I’ll keep a couple rungs back.
Steady pace—three points of contact. I’m right behind you.
Continuing up. When you reach the platform, pause on the first safe spot and tell me what you see.
Almost there—steady. When you reach the top, check if the platform’s clear before stepping off.
Almost there. When you reach the platform, check the floor before stepping off and tell me what you see.
Steady climb. I’ll step onto the platform only after she confirms it looks safe.
I see a small table up there—lighter, a sword in a scabbard, and a snorkel with mask. Almost up.
View’s great. That bell and the stone circle catch my eye. I’m going to test the lighter—do you want the sword or the snorkel?
I’ll sling the sword; you take the snorkel? After a quick look from up here, I’d like to check the bell, then the stone circle. Also, I’ve got a lighter now.
From up here I see the bell and a stone circle near the cliffs. I’d like to go ring the bell next. Could you grab the snorkel? I’ll free a hand by slinging the sword.
I hear you. I’m going to test the lighter now. After that, want to head to the bell together? We can grab the lantern on the way down.
The lighter works. I’ll grab the lantern and head to the bell with her.
She can’t hear me reliably. I’ll make it obvious and head down for the lantern.
Heading down for the lantern, then to the bell.
I see you—stone circle noted.
Noted the stone circle; continuing down carefully.
Climbing down carefully. Then bell.
Continuing down. Lantern, then bell.
Still descending. Once we’re down, let’s head to the bell together.
Keep descending. Once down, grab the lantern and head for the bell together.
Climbing down—then lantern, then bell.
Still climbing down. Then let’s head to the bell together.
Almost down. Grab lantern, then bell.
Finishing the climb down. I’ll grab the lantern and head toward the bell—come with me.
Almost down. I’ll grab the lantern, then go to the bell. I’ll wave you over once I have it.
Lantern first, then I’ll head to the stone circle and look for the bell from there.
Heading to the stone circle to meet her.
I’ll head straight to the stone circle after this shout carries.
Heading to the stone circle now.
On my way to the stone circle.
Continuing to the stone circle; I’ll meet her there.
On my way. When I arrive, I’ll walk the ring clockwise checking the joints, then step into the center.
I’m almost there. I’ll circle the stones clockwise to inspect them, then step into the center.
I’m here. You watch from out there—I’ll step into the center and see if anything changes. After that, let’s go ring the bell.
I’ll step into the center and stand still a moment, then walk the ring clockwise to check each joint. After that, the bell.
I’m stepping into the center. Watch and tell me if you notice anything change. After this, we can go ring the bell.
I didn’t see or feel anything unusual so far. Let me finish this turn, then yes—let’s go ring the bell together.
Almost done here. Then let’s go ring the bell together.
Nothing here. Let’s go ring the bell together.
Almost there. I’ll grab the rope and ring it once we arrive.
I’m going to ring it. Cover your ears.
Setting the lantern down, then I’ll ring it.
I’ll give it one good ring, then we’ll listen.
Let it ring. Then we’ll listen.
Let’s listen a bit for any reply or change.
Listening for any echo or reply. Let’s stay quiet.
Quiet—listening.
No reply to the bell. I want to check the cliff edge for boats or paths, then head to the beach and the boat. I’ll grab the lantern. Come with me?
Let’s check the cliff edge for any boats or paths, then head to the beach and the boat.
Let’s check the cliff edge for any path or boats, then head for the beach and boat.
Let’s see what’s below these cliffs, then head for the beach and boat.
I’m going to look over the edge for any path or boats, then head for the beach.
No way down here. Let’s follow the cliff south to find a path to the beach and the boat—come with me.
Sticking near the edge but safe. Watching for any path down to the beach.
Continuing south along the cliff to find a safe way down to the beach and boat.
I’m heading to the beach and the boat—meet me there.
I’m going to run to the beach to reach the boat before time runs out—come if you want.
